kaps_punt: Hantering van emosies: empatie, deernis, woede, teleurstelling en hartseer

items.bewering: Jou lyf weet dikwels eerste dat jy kwaad word.
items.bron: Care for the Family (UK charity), 'When tempers flare: helping children manage anger': 'Often our bodies notice it before our minds do'. Nemours KidsHealth 'Taking Charge of Anger (for Kids)' ('Your body will tell you when you are angry'). Therapist Aid 'Anger Stop Signs' uses the same idea of body warning signs. 'dikwels' keeps it from claiming this always happens. Checked on the web this round.

items.bewering: Jou hart klop vinniger en jou spiere trek styf oor jou skouers.
items.bron: Nemours KidsHealth (kids), anger: tense muscles, faster breathing. Nummenmaa et al. 2014, 'Bodily maps of emotions', PNAS 111:646-651: anger is felt mainly in the upper torso, arms and head. General anger-physiology sources agree: faster heartbeat, tense neck and shoulder muscles.

items.bewering: Jou stem raak harder sonder dat jy dit besluit het.
items.bron: Several anger-physiology overviews list a louder voice as an automatic sign of anger, as part of the fight-or-flight response. Care for the Family: anger 'can sneak up on you'. The claim is about a reaction you do not choose, and it is consistent with these sources.

items.bewering: Woede kom op wanneer iets jou seermaak of wanneer iets vir jou onbillik voel.
items.bron: American Psychological Association (apa.org/topics/anger/control): anger is a normal response to a threat. Summaries of the APA and Mind (mind.org.uk) guidance say anger usually comes from a perceived threat, insult or injustice, and some people use anger to avoid feeling hurt. 'wanneer' is not framed as 'only when', so the claim is not too strong.

items.bewering: Woede self is nie 'n verkeerde gevoel nie. Wat jy met die woede doen, kan wel verkeerd wees.
items.bron: American Psychological Association: 'Anger is a completely normal, usually healthy, human emotion'. Mind (UK) and Better Health Channel (Victoria State Government): the problem is how you express it, not the feeling itself.

items.bewering: 'n Kind wat kwaad word en dan slaan, maak 'n ander kind seer.
items.bron: Self-evident. It is also in line with APA and Mind guidance that expressing anger in harmful ways hurts other people. Recorded to show it was looked at.

items.bewering: Teleurstelling kom wanneer iets waarop jy gehoop het, nie gebeur nie.
items.bron: Oxford Pocket Dictionary of Current English (via Encyclopedia.com): disappointment is 'the feeling of sadness or displeasure caused by the nonfulfilment of one's hopes or expectations'. Cambridge Dictionary gives the same.

items.bewering: Jou keel voel toe en jy wil nie eers met iemand praat nie.
items.bron: BBC Science Focus ('why you get a lump in your throat when you're about to cry') and Cleveland Clinic ('Globus sensation'): a tight throat is a common short-lived feeling in sadness, grief and strong emotion. Zeelenberg, van Dijk & Manstead 1998, 'The experience of regret and disappointment', Cognition & Emotion 12:221-230: disappointment comes with feeling powerless and wanting to get away from the situation, which supports not wanting to talk.

items.bewering: Hierdie gevoel is stiller as woede en ander mense sien dit nie altyd nie.
items.bron: Frijda et al. 1989 (via Lerner et al., 'Emotion and Decision Making', and the Frijda legacy article in Cognition & Emotion): anger makes you want to act against something. Zeelenberg et al. 1998: disappointment makes you feel powerless and want to withdraw. Low arousal and withdrawal fit 'stiller'. 'nie altyd nie' is a modest claim.

items.bewering: Hartseer kom wanneer jy iets of iemand verloor wat vir jou kosbaar is.
items.bron: Appraisal theory (Lazarus; summarised in Lerner et al., 'Emotion and Decision Making'): the core theme of sadness is irrevocable loss. The sentence does not say sadness comes ONLY from loss.

items.bewering: Dikwels voel jou lyf swaar en moeg en wil jy nie speel nie.
items.bron: Nummenmaa et al. 2014, PNAS: sadness reduces feeling in the limbs and makes people reluctant to move. AACAP 'Grief and Children' and grief-support sources: children who are grieving may have less energy than usual and pull back from their normal activities.

items.bewering: Hartseer wys nie by almal op dieselfde manier nie. Een kind huil sommer dadelik en 'n ander kind word baie stil. Nog 'n kind word kwaad vir almal om hom en weet self nie hoekom nie. Al drie is hartseer en niemand van hulle doen dit verkeerd nie.
items.bron: American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, 'Grief and Children' (Facts for Families): grieving children react in different ways, including anger and irritability. Red Nose Australia, 'Children's grief reactions': a child may cry all the time, now and then, or not at all, and all of these are normal. Understood.org, 'Why kids grieve in unexpected ways'. Grief support services agree that anger and irritability are a normal form of children's grief.

items.bewering: Noem die gevoel by sy naam en sê vir jouself jy is kwaad.
items.blok: Wat jy met 'n groot gevoel kan doen
items.bron: Lieberman et al. 2007, 'Putting Feelings Into Words', Psychological Science 18:421-428: putting a name to a feeling reduced amygdala activity. UCLA Health press release on the same study. Kircanski, Lieberman & Craske 2012: naming a feeling reduced the body's response.

items.bewering: Wag voor jy praat as die woede opkom en stap weg tot jy kalmer is. Loop tot by die hek en kom terug.
items.blok: Wat jy met 'n groot gevoel kan doen
items.bron: Nemours KidsHealth, 'Taming Tempers': teach children it is OK to walk away to calm down. Stanford Medicine Children's Health and Child Mind Institute: wait until you are calm before talking, and use a break.

items.bewering: Sê dit vir iemand. Baie kinders voel ligter nadat hulle die teleurstelling hardop gesê het.
items.blok: Wat jy met 'n groot gevoel kan doen
items.bron: Nemours KidsHealth, Teacher's Guide 'Feeling Sad (Grades 3 to 5)', and The Kids Mental Health Foundation: telling someone how you feel helps and shows you are not alone. The affect-labeling research (Lieberman 2007) backs the same thing. Note: I found no source that measures this for disappointment in children specifically. 'Baie' is a modest quantifier and the general evidence supports it, so it is not marked uncertain.

items.bewering: Doen iets met jou lyf as die hartseer swaar sit. Hardloop of maak die erf skoon.
items.blok: Wat jy met 'n groot gevoel kan doen
items.bron: Systematic review and meta-analysis, 'The Effects of Physical Activity on Positive Emotions in Children and Adolescents' (PMC9657539): physical activity significantly improves children's mood. Nuffield Health, children's mental health and exercise.

items.bewering: Jy kan nie in sy kop sien nie, maar jy kan jou in sy plek dink. Empatie is om te verstaan hoe iemand anders voel en saam met hom te voel. Dan kan jy raai wat nou binne-in hom aangaan.
items.blok: Om in iemand anders se plek te dink
items.bron: Singer & Klimecki 2014, 'Empathy and compassion', Current Biology 24(18): empathy is the ability to take another person's point of view and feel their emotions ('feeling with'). The lesson's definition covers both parts, understanding and feeling with. 'raai' honestly says you cannot know for certain.

items.bewering: Empatie laat jou saamvoel met die maat op die trap. Dit beteken nie vanself dat jy hom wil help nie. By deernis voel jy vir hom en jy wil hom help.
items.blok: Voel vir hom en wil help
items.bron: Singer & Klimecki 2014, Current Biology: empathy is 'feeling with' and compassion is 'feeling for'. Compassion includes a strong wish to help, which is 'not commonly considered part of empathy'. Global Compassion Coalition and Naropa University say the same. The distinction the lesson draws is exactly the one in the research.

items.bewering: Jou hande wys dit gewoonlik, soos wanneer jy langs hom gaan sit of jou kospakkie deel.
items.blok: Voel vir hom en wil help
items.bron: Singer & Klimecki 2014: compassion leads to action, and empathic distress leads to withdrawal. Sitting beside someone and sharing are examples of helping in practice. 'gewoonlik' does not claim this always happens.

items.bewering: 'n Maat kan nie 'n oupa terugbring nie en hy kan nie keer dat 'n gesin wegtrek nie. Hy kan wel bly waar sy maat is. Hy luister sonder om die gesprek na sy eie storie toe te draai. Hulle hou aan met die gewone dinge soos brood deel en saam huis toe loop. 'n Maat hoef niks reg te maak nie.
items.bron: Dougy Center, 'Your Friend is Grieving': grieving friends do not need you to fix their grief, but to 'show up, stick around, act normal, and listen'. HelpGuide, 'Helping someone who is grieving': do not make it about yourself, and offer practical help. JMU Counseling Center, 'Helping a Grieving Friend'.

items.bewering: Hy dra dit ook nie alleen nie. Sê dit vir 'n grootmens wat jy vertrou as jou maat lank swaarkry of as hy in gevaar is. Dit kan die grootmens by die huis wees, 'n onderwyser of 'n verpleegster by die kliniek.
items.bron: Childline South Africa, 'Extracts from Prevention & Education Manual' (disclosure of child abuse): a child can tell a parent, teacher, doctor, relative, social worker and others. Department of Health knowledge hub, 'Mandatory reporting of child abuse in terms of the Children's Act': nurses and teachers are legally required to report abuse, so a clinic nurse is a correct South African example of an adult who must act. AACAP 'Grief and Children': long-lasting difficulty is a sign to get adult help.

items.bewering: As die eerste een nie luister nie, gaan vra die volgende een.
items.bron: Childline Mpumalanga, 'Info for Children': 'you keep telling until someone believes you and does something about the abuse', and if the adult gets angry 'you need to tell another adult'. Childline South Africa's Rule 6: 'Keep telling people you trust ... until someone listens'. 'eerste' here is an ordinal, not a historical superlative. It is listed so the superlative sweep is complete.

items.bewering: emosie: 'n Sterk gevoel binne-in jou, soos woede, hartseer of blydskap.
items.bron: Cambridge Dictionary: emotion is 'a strong feeling such as love or anger'. Collins English Dictionary lists happiness, anger and others as emotions. Read on its own, the entry is correct and does not fit something that is not an emotion.

items.bewering: woede: Die warm, gespanne gevoel wat jou wil laat terugstoot as iets seermaak of onbillik voel.
items.bron: Frijda et al. 1989 (via Lerner et al., 'Emotion and Decision Making'): anger makes you want to 'move against' and resist its cause, which is 'terugstoot'. Nummenmaa et al. 2014: anger is felt as heightened sensation in the upper body, and anger-physiology sources mention flushing and tense muscles, which supports 'warm, gespanne'. The APA and Mind summaries give hurt and injustice as causes.

items.bewering: teleurstelling: Die gevoel wanneer iets waarop jy gehoop het, nie gebeur nie.
items.bron: Oxford Pocket Dictionary of Current English and Cambridge Dictionary, disappointment: the feeling when hopes or expectations are not fulfilled.

items.bewering: hartseer: Die swaar gevoel wat kom as jy iets of iemand verloor.
items.bron: Appraisal theory (Lazarus, via Lerner et al.): the core theme of sadness is irrevocable loss. Nummenmaa et al. 2014: sadness is felt as less activity and heaviness in the body, which supports 'swaar'. Read on its own, the entry is correct.

items.bewering: empatie: Verstaan en saamvoel deur jou in iemand anders se plek te dink.
items.bron: Singer & Klimecki 2014, Current Biology: empathy is taking another person's point of view and feeling their emotions. The entry has both parts and does not claim that empathy includes wanting to help, so it does not overlap with deernis.

items.bewering: deernis: Om vir iemand wat swaarkry te voel en hom te wil help.
items.bron: Supertaal dictionary (gesellig.co.za), 'deernis': ''n Diep meegevoel of medelye', translated as compassion. Singer & Klimecki 2014: compassion is feeling for someone who is suffering plus the motivation to help. The dictionary meaning and the psychological meaning together support the entry.

opsomming: All 28 claims were checked against the web and confirmed. The lesson has no ELI10 blocks and no analogies to check, its two uses of 'eerste' hold up, and the one claim with only indirect evidence (that 'baie kinders' feel lighter after saying their disappointment out loud) rests on general research about talking about feelings rather than a study of children and disappointment.
